- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay correction until 2–3 days after sentiment turns neutral.
- After a spike in price (forecast > 75), model tends to overcorrect — apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion to prevent premature decline.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast and avoid overfitting to recent noise.
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days), apply a 2–3% downward bias adjustment for next period, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently bullish but price fails to rise beyond 75, reduce forecast ceiling by 5–8% to account for market saturation or policy caps.
